title: Introduction to Azure App Service
description: Understand App Service plans, deployment slots, and scaling options for web apps and APIs.

data.text: **Azure App Service** is a fully managed platform for hosting web applications, REST APIs, and mobile back ends. Unlike VMs, you do not manage the underlying servers. You simply upload your code, and Azure handles the operating system, patching, and infrastructure.

An **App Service plan** defines the set of compute resources for your app. Think of it as the hardware behind your app. One plan can run multiple apps, and you can scale the plan up or down as needed.

data.title: Plan Tiers at a Glance
items: **Free / Shared**: Good for testing. Limited CPU and no custom domain.
**Basic**: Production-ready basics. Custom domains and SSL supported.
**Standard**: Auto-scaling, staging slots, and daily backups.
**Premium / Isolated**: Maximum scale, isolated compute, and virtual network integration.

data.text: **Deployment slots** are live apps with their own hostnames. You can use a slot to stage a new version, test it, and then swap it into production without downtime.

data.title: Deploy to a Slot Using Azure CLI
data.content: Create a deployment slot and push your code to it.
data.code:
az webapp deployment slot create \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp \
  --slot staging

az webapp deployment source config-zip \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp \
  --slot staging \
  --src myapp.zip

data.text: You can scale an App Service plan in two ways: scale up to a bigger plan with more CPU and memory, or scale out to add more instances running the same plan.

rows: Move to a higher tier (e.g., Standard to Premium)
Your app needs more CPU, memory, or features
Add more instances of the same plan
Your app needs to handle more users or requests

terms.definition: The set of compute resources that host one or more App Service apps.
A separate app environment used for staging and swapping.
Increase the resources of a plan by moving to a higher tier.
Add more instances of the same plan to handle more traffic.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Always test new versions in a staging slot before swapping into production. If something goes wrong, you can swap back instantly.

data.title: Exercise: Plan an App Service Deployment
data.description: Choose the right App Service tier and scaling strategy for a given scenario.
steps: An internal company dashboard used by 50 people during business hours.
A public e-commerce site expecting 10,000 visitors during a sale.
A small API for a mobile app used by 200 daily active users.
data.expectedOutcome: You can match app traffic and requirements to Basic, Standard, or Premium tiers and decide when to scale out.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: App Service is a managed platform for web apps and APIs.
The App Service plan defines the underlying compute resources.
Deployment slots let you stage and test changes safely.
You can scale up for more power or scale out for more capacity.
data.takeaway: App Service removes server management overhead while still giving you control over scaling and deployment behavior.
